title: Guidelines on Ensuring AI Transparency
summary: MSIT guidance released on 21–22 January 2026, alongside the AI Basic Act's entry into force, explaining how operators can meet the transparency duty in Article 31. A draft was published in September 2025. It describes acceptable ways to give advance notice that a service uses high-impact or generative AI, how to label AI outputs inside and outside a service, and how to mark deepfakes. It covers operators, including foreign ones, that offer AI products directly to users in Korea, but not people who only use AI as a creative tool. The guidance is not itself binding.
key_obligations: Give advance notice via terms, contracts, app screens or offline notices
Outputs used within a service may be flagged by UI labels or logos
Outputs exported or shared need a watermark or machine-readable metadata
Deepfakes must be labelled so users clearly recognise them

sources.title: MSIT Releases Guidelines on Ensuring AI Transparency
